nodes.label: Force Lexical Retrieval Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: A persisted runtime switch restores lexical behavior without reinstalling or deleting the semantic index.

nodes.label: Local Bundled Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Historical meeting text must not be sent to an embedding API.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.rationale: BM25, cosine, and query-variant scores are not numerically comparable.

nodes.label: Hybrid RAG Authority Order
nodes.rationale: Material conflicts must be recorded and approved rather than silently resolved.

nodes.label: Platform Build Acceleration
nodes.rationale: Windows enables Vulkan GPU acceleration, Linux uses OpenBLAS because GitHub-hosted Linux runners have no GPUs, and macOS uses Metal by default.

nodes.label: DevTest Build Guidance
nodes.rationale: Code signing is disabled by default to speed development and testing builds, while allowing it to be opted into for production-like testing.

nodes.label: Supported Tauri Application API
nodes.rationale: The Next.js UI communicates with the Rust core through Tauri commands and events.

nodes.label: Legacy Backend Archive
nodes.rationale: The Python/FastAPI, Docker, and standalone whisper-server implementation is retained only for historical reference and is unsupported for the current application.

nodes.label: On-Device Data Privacy
nodes.rationale: Usage analytics collect no personal content, and all content remains on the user's device.

nodes.label: Unified Application Data Storage
nodes.rationale: Database and models are stored together in the application data directory for unified management.

nodes.label: APIs (Ollama with Agentic Tools)
nodes.rationale: Use small LLMs where possible.

nodes.label: Privacy First AI Copilot for Meeting Notes
nodes.norm_label: privacy first ai copilot for meeting notes

nodes.label: Bluetooth Playback Limitations
nodes.rationale: The recording file remains correct; distortion, pitch shifts, and speed changes occur in Bluetooth playback.

nodes.label: Wired Playback Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Computer speakers, wired headphones, and high-quality DACs avoid the Bluetooth sample-rate conversion problem during recording review.

nodes.label: FTS5 Search Index
nodes.rationale: FTS5 replaces a LIKE full-table scan and unicode61 avoids Portuguese stemming errors.

nodes.label: MCP Server
nodes.rationale: The plan selects axum and serde_json to avoid SDK bloat while reusing Tokio.

nodes.label: File Upload Security Warning
nodes.rationale: The server accepts user uploads and may invoke ffmpeg conversions, so it must not run with administrative privileges.

nodes.label: Exact Vector Search
nodes.rationale: Exact search passed the 250k latency and memory gates, so ANN was neither needed nor permitted.

nodes.label: Local-First Processing
nodes.rationale: Transcription and meeting content stay on user-controlled infrastructure.

nodes.label: Privacy-First Commitment
nodes.rationale: Meeting data remains private and under user control.

nodes.label: F1 Custom Summary Templates
nodes.rationale: User-authored templates are a core productivity feature and their structure is reused by exports and integrations.

nodes.label: Local Processing Privacy Guarantee
nodes.rationale: Transcription, diarization, summarization, and chat remain local or use the user's configured LLM endpoint; outbound Notion delivery requires an explicit action.

nodes.label: No Analytics
nodes.rationale: The analytics module is removed so no analytics event is emitted by the additions.

nodes.label: F10 Encrypted API Key Storage
nodes.rationale: The upstream application stores API keys in plaintext; encryption must be implemented before integrations introduce additional credentials.

nodes.label: F11 Meeting Notes Editor
nodes.rationale: The table and BlockNote editor already exist upstream, making database wiring a small, useful implementation.

nodes.label: Disabled Tauri Auto-Updater
nodes.rationale: Updates are deferred to an internal channel because the Tauri auto-updater is disabled.

nodes.label: Dead audio_v2 Module
nodes.rationale: The directory exists but is not declared in lib.rs or referenced, so F4 and F5 must use audio/ or newly declared top-level modules.

nodes.label: DiariZen
nodes.rationale: DiariZen is excluded because its CC BY-NC 4.0 weights are non-commercial and unsafe for a shared team build.

nodes.label: reverb-diarization-v1
nodes.rationale: This sherpa-onnx segmentation alternative is excluded because its license is non-commercial.

nodes.label: Full Local Ownership
nodes.rationale: The fork avoids license servers, telemetry, vendor lock-in, and non-explicit cloud processing.

nodes.label: Local ONNX and GGUF Model Storage
nodes.norm_label: local onnx and gguf model storage

nodes.label: Retrieval Model Release Gate
nodes.rationale: The CI workflow stages verified retrieval artifacts and runs stable, finite, dimensional reference inference before the Windows application build.

nodes.label: External Cargo Target Directory
nodes.rationale: Cargo artifacts must be outside the OneDrive repository and the target directory must be explicitly set per shell.

nodes.label: Smart App Control Build Blocker
nodes.rationale: Enforced Smart App Control blocks unsigned Rust build scripts, so local Rust compilation must wait for it to be disabled or move to CI.

nodes.label: 3D-Speaker ERes2Net
nodes.rationale: The multilingual embedding model is preferred for PT-BR, subject to a Portuguese meeting smoke test before it is locked.

nodes.label: diarize FoxNoseTech
nodes.rationale: It is retained only as a fallback if its ONNX bundle and Apache-2.0 weights are independently confirmed.

nodes.label: diart
nodes.rationale: It is the future option only if live speaker labels become mandatory and the CC-BY-4.0 attribution requirement is acceptable.

nodes.label: sherpa-onnx
nodes.rationale: sherpa-onnx is the locked primary because it is ONNX-native, avoids a Python runtime, has Rust and Tauri integration paths, delivers a turnkey pipeline, and runs faster than real time on CPU.

nodes.label: Local Hybrid Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Global ranking returned isolated FTS snippets while complete answers remained unread, so retrieval must rank meetings first and hydrate authoritative content rather than rely on a prompt change.

nodes.label: Phase 5 Meeting Context and Relationship Memory
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 meeting context and relationship memory

nodes.label: Windows x64 Retrieval Scope
nodes.rationale: Only the root Windows workflow is active; requiring macOS and Linux packaged inference made the retrieval gate unsatisfiable.

nodes.label: F4 Auto-Detect Meetings
nodes.rationale: Auto-start is explicitly opt-in and visibly announced to prevent covert recording.
